name: Post Training Quantization of Large Language Models with Microscaling Formats
problem: SmoothQuant, AWQ and GPTQ were each designed for fixed-point targets; none of them can emit the microscaling formats that new hardware natively supports.
mechanism: Extends SmoothQuant, AWQ and GPTQ so each can quantize into MX formats (shared per-block power-of-two scale plus a narrow element type), and then studies how the three compose when stacked: activation smoothing (SmoothQuant) before activation-aware weight saliency (AWQ) before error-compensating rounding (GPTQ). The contribution is largely the compatibility work plus the interaction analysis, not a new algorithm.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): combining the PTQ methods allows quantizing to 4-bit weights and 8-bit activations in the MXINT format 'with negligible accuracy loss compared to the uncompressed baseline'. COMPRESSION RATIO: 4-bit weights + 8-bit activations in MXINT (~4x on weights vs FP16, plus the shared-scale overhead). QUALITY COST: 'negligible' - no paired delta in the abstract.
